summary:
Josip Torbar (1889–1963) was a Croatian lawyer and Croatian Peasant Party (HSS) politician who held senior party roles and served as a Yugoslav government minister. A member of parliament, he became minister of posts, telegraph and telephone after the 1939 agreement that gave Croatia autonomy within Yugoslavia.

During World War II, the Ustaše regime banned the HSS and detained its leader, Vladko Maček. Torbar met several times with regime leader Ante Pavelić, seeking better conditions for the party, the release of its members, and changes to Ustaše policies. In 1943–44, he helped plan the Lorković–Vokić plot to remove Pavelić, disarm German forces and bring the HSS to power with Western Allied support. The plot failed, and Torbar was imprisoned.

Released in May 1945, he fled through Europe and South America to Canada and the United States. He died in New York City in 1963.
